item.title: NSCIA to politicians: Keep 2027 campaign violence out of mosques
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA) has condemned attacks in and around some mosques, warning politicians and other actors against using places of worship as grounds for violence and confrontation ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Council said no political disagreement, doctrinal differences or personal grievances could justify violence against worshippers, insisting that mosques must remain sanctuaries of worship and peace, not arenas for settling disputes. The warning was contained in a statement by the NSCIA Secretary-General, Prof. Ishaq Oloyede, on behalf of the Council, led by its President-General, the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar. Describing the attacks as reprehensible and fundamentally contrary to Islamic teachings, the Council stressed that every Muslim had a duty to respect the sanctity of mosques and protect the lives and dignity of worshippers. “These teachings leave no room for violence, intimidation, harassment, assault, attack on or threat against people’s safety and lives in the name of doctrinal differences, political disagreement, socio-economic grievance or any other cause,” it said. The NSCIA maintained that all Muslims had equal rights in mosques and that no worshipper should be intimidated, harassed or attacked under any guise within or around mosque premises. In a specific demand for action against those responsible, the Council urged mosque authorities to assist in identifying perpetrators and provide video recordings of the incidents to law enforcement agencies to facilitate their arrest. It also urged Muslims with grievances to seek redress through dialogue, constructive advocacy, lawful engagement and the courts rather than resorting to violence. “No grievance, however genuine or contrived for expediency, should become a justification for violence or the violation of human dignity or the desecration of the Houses of Allah,” the Council declared. Citing the Qur’an’s injunction against aggression, the NSCIA reminded Muslims of the directive to “cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression” (Qur’an 5:2). The Council also cautioned political actors across party lines, religious leaders, community leaders and members of the public against inflammatory statements and actions capable of escalating tensions or threatening public peace. “They should also stop, henceforth, from desecrating the mosques through acts of violence and desist from embarrassing the nation,” it said. Reaffirming its commitment to peace, justice, dialogue and national unity, the NSCIA said it would continue engaging the government, security agencies and other stakeholders to protect religious freedoms and promote national stability. The Council prayed for the recovery of those injured, comfort for affected persons and lasting peace, security and justice in Nigeria. item.title: Simeone sets La Liga record with 345 wins for Atletico Madrid
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Diego Simeone became the manager with the most victories in La Liga history after Atletico Madrid’s 3-0 victory over Getafe on Sunday, taking his tally to 345 wins in the Spanish top flight. Atletico confirmed the milestone in a statement, saying Simeone had moved past club legend Luis Aragonés, who finished his La Liga career with 344 victories. Simeone reached the record in 189 fewer matches than Aragonés. The 56-year-old said he was pleased with the achievement and pointed to the work behind it. “It makes me happy,” Simeone said. “I don’t usually find many things to be happy about, but there is an incredible amount of work behind this.” Atletico said Simeone has won 60 per cent of the league matches he has managed. The Argentine has led the club since December 2011, when Barcelona and Real Madrid were the dominant sides in Spain. Asked about the criticism that his teams are too defensive, Simeone said it was a constant narrative but questioned whether defence alone could account for his record. “This narrative that we’re a defensive team, as if we’re always playing solely to defend. You don’t win 345 matches just by defending. Is that even possible?” he said. Simeone has also won eight trophies with Atletico: two La Liga titles, one Copa del Rey, one Spanish Super Cup, two UEFA Super Cups and two Europa League crowns. The club noted that he has won two more trophies than Aragonés did during his time in charge. His first silverware came in 2012, when Atletico won the Europa League and then the UEFA Super Cup. He guided them to the Copa del Rey in his first full season and their first La Liga title since 1996 the following campaign. Atletico won another league title under him in 2021 and completed a Europa League and UEFA Super Cup double in 2018. Simeone has also taken Atletico to two Champions League finals, losing to city rivals Real Madrid in 2014 and 2016. Atletico have qualified for the Champions League in every full season of his tenure. The record was set as Atletico moved to third in the table after 10 wins from 13 matches. The 56-year-old’s contract expires at the end of the season. The post Simeone sets La Liga record with 345 wins for Atletico Madrid appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 4 facilities FIFA President says Nigeria must fix to host FIFA World Cup
item.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has identified four key infrastructure areas Nigeria must improve to strengthen its chances of hosting the FIFA World Cup in the future. Infantino listed stadiums, hotels, airports and transportation as critical requirements for hosting the global football competition, noting that Nigeria has the resources and potential to pursue the ambition. He made the remarks during an interview with Arise TV, where he assessed Nigeria’s readiness to host the tournament. According to him, although Nigeria is currently not ready to host the competition, ongoing and proposed infrastructure projects could provide a foundation for future ambitions. “Well, the next World Cup will be co-hosted by Morocco, so the World Cup comes back to Africa. The key for hosting the World Cup is the infrastructures: the stadiums, hotels, airports, transportation, and this is where the investment is really needed,” he said. 1. Stadiums Infantino said Nigeria needs to invest in stadium infrastructure, acknowledging ongoing and proposed stadium construction projects across the country. He cited his visits to the National Stadium training centre in Abuja and a stadium in Warri, describing the latter as nice but small. “I visited the National stadium training centre in Abuja, In Warri as well, nice stadium, though small stadium,” he said. 2. Hotels Adequate hotel infrastructure is another requirement for hosting the World Cup. Nigeria would need sufficient accommodation facilities to cater to visiting teams, officials, journalists, supporters and other international visitors. 3. Airports Airport infrastructure is also essential to receiving and facilitating the movement of thousands of international visitors expected during the tournament. 4. Transportation Efficient transportation networks would be needed to connect airports, hotels, stadiums and other tournament facilities, ensuring the smooth movement of teams, officials and spectators. Infantino acknowledged Nigeria’s potential, citing its resources, football passion and willingness to invest in infrastructure. He added that the country could build towards hosting the competition by identifying achievable starting points and gradually expanding its infrastructure capacity. On whether Nigeria was currently ready to host the tournament, Infantino said: “Today, no Nigeria is not ready, but tomorrow, why not? When I look at what is being projected, Nigeria has all its cards in its own hands.” Vanguard News The post 4 facilities FIFA President says Nigeria must fix to host FIFA World Cup appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Ogun Accord rejects coalition, says party not for sale
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State chapter of the Accord Party has dismissed claims of a political coalition or endorsement deal with any party ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that it is not for sale and remains committed to contesting elections at all levels. The party also warned individuals and groups against using its name to negotiate political alliances or endorse candidates of other parties without the authorisation of its recognised state leadership. The State Chairman, Oke Rotimi Michael, stated this in a statement, insisting that the party had neither entered into a coalition nor reached any agreement to support another political party or its candidates. He said Accord remained committed to its political philosophy, vision and mission of providing credible leadership, promoting people-centred governance and improving the welfare of residents of the state. Michael warned that the party would not allow itself to become an instrument of political bargaining, personal ambition or clandestine negotiations by individuals seeking to advance interests outside its recognised structure. He described Accord as an ideological political platform with a distinct identity and a commitment to the aspirations, economic well-being, security and future of the people. “ACCORD is not a political party built on selfish interests, desperation for power, political bargaining or opportunistic alliances. We are a party with an identity, a mission and a clearly defined vision of providing credible political leadership that will empower Nigerians and improve the living conditions of our people. “Our commitment to people-centred politics is fundamental to who we are. The aspirations of the people, their economic survival, security and future remain at the heart of our political philosophy. These values are not negotiable,” he said. The chairman acknowledged that political consultations, lobbying and negotiations were legitimate aspects of democratic practice but maintained that nobody had the authority to negotiate away the party’s identity, interests or electoral prospects without the approval of its recognised leadership. He also cautioned against attempts by individuals to persuade or induce the party’s candidates to endorse candidates of other political parties outside its established decision-making process. “Let me make it categorically clear: ACCORD Ogun State is not for sale. We have not entered into any political coalition, nor have we reached an agreement to support another political party or its candidates. “Any purported coalition arrangement, political endorsement, agreement or understanding entered into by any individual or group without the authorisation and consent of the recognised Ogun State party leadership under my chairmanship does not represent the position of ACCORD Ogun State,” he said. item.title: Fani-Kayode demands action over Nigerians’ deaths in South Africa
item.description: Nigeria’s Ambassador to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has called for urgent action over unresolved cases involving the deaths of Nigerians in the country, alleged misconduct by security personnel and growing anti-Nigerian sentiments. Fani-Kayode, in a statement on Monday, said the protection of Nigerians living in South Africa must remain a priority of his diplomatic mission, warning that the pursuit of stronger bilateral relations should not come at the expense of citizens’ safety and welfare. The concerns come amid reports that at least 12 Nigerians have died in South Africa in 2026 in incidents linked to anti-migrant protests, alleged police brutality and attacks reportedly motivated by Afrophobia. The ambassador said Nigeria remained committed to strengthening diplomatic and economic ties with South Africa but would not remain silent over issues threatening the safety, dignity and rights of its citizens. He described relations between the two countries as critical to Africa’s economic integration, political stability and development, noting that cooperation between the continent’s two leading economies was essential to its progress. “The future of Africa is closely tied to the relationship between Nigeria and South Africa. If these two countries fail to work together, it could have significant implications for the continent’s progress,” he said. Fani-Kayode said he had consistently advocated dialogue, mutual respect and stronger bilateral engagement since assuming office. However, he maintained that cordial relations between the two governments should not prevent Nigeria from raising legitimate concerns about the treatment of its citizens. He specifically identified unresolved deaths involving Nigerians, alleged misconduct by some South African security personnel and anti-Nigerian statements by certain groups as matters requiring urgent attention. The envoy also warned against portraying the entire Nigerian community in South Africa negatively because of the alleged criminal activities of a few individuals. He said thousands of Nigerians in the country were law-abiding professionals and entrepreneurs whose contributions should not be undermined by the conduct of a minority. “Thousands of Nigerians in South Africa are law-abiding professionals, including doctors, lawyers, academics and entrepreneurs. A small minority engaged in wrongdoing should not be used to define an entire community,” he said. He further cautioned against treating anti-Nigerian rhetoric from some organisations as representative of the views of the wider South African population. Nevertheless, he described expressions of hostility towards Nigerians as troubling and called for sustained dialogue and engagement to address tensions between the two communities. item.title: Fury reveals schizophrenia diagnosis ahead of Joshua clash
item.description: Tyson Fury has said he was diagnosed with schizophrenia soon after his world title win over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” said the heavyweight boxer. “It was like a living version of the pits of hell. “I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much. “The anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it and that’s when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London.” Fury has made the revelations about his mental health in a documentary which will be released by Netflix on Friday. The 38-year-old is preparing for the long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight against Anthony Joshua, a fellow former world champion, in Cardiff on December 11 — a bout that will be broadcast live on Netflix. Fury recalled hearing the radio talking to him, and begging wife Paris to get him out of the hospital because “the Illuminati” wanted him. Following his victory over Klitschko, Fury gained weight and struggled with alcohol and drug addiction. “It got that bad I was hearing voices in my mind,” he said. “I wouldn’t be able to sit and have a conversation because I’d be hearing stuff in my mind. “I didn’t know where to turn and no-one knew what to do. I really needed help, or check into rehab or something. I never got a break from it for years. I wanted to be what I thought was normal again.” After Fury was released from hospital, a diagnosis of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder was confirmed. Fury said a turning point in his life came when he was on a night out for Halloween in 2017. “I looked around and could see all the young people and I thought, ‘I had the world in my hands and I threw it all away, and now I’m a fat mess addicted to alcohol’,” he said. But Fury added he channelled his disgust into a comeback which led him to return to training, focus more on his family and claim another world title when he beat Deontay Wilder in 2020. item.title: Why I will never forget Daniel Amokachi – Hull City owner
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Hull City owner Acun Ilıcalı has revealed how his close friendship with former Nigerian international Daniel Amokachi began during the striker’s spell at Turkish club Besiktas, describing their relationship as one that made them “brothers”. Ilıcalı, who was a football reporter covering Besiktas at the time, recalled how he became so close to the club’s players that the coach would sometimes approach him to find out their whereabouts. While speaking on The Overlap Podcast, the Turkish businessman singled out Amokachi as one of the players he shared a particularly close relationship with, adding that the Nigerian trusted him more than other journalists. “One memory from that time I will never forget is Daniel Amokachi. He had played for Everton, so we became brothers with him. Amokachi spoke only to me and nobody else. All the reporters were asking me to let Amokachi speak to them,” Ilıcalı said. He also recalled how much the former Super Eagles striker trusted him, revealing that Amokachi would leave his Mercedes-Benz 500 SL with him whenever he travelled to Nigeria. “He trusted me so much that he would leave his 500 SL when he went to Nigeria. I would drive it to work, and the whole company was shocked. Everyone would ask what it was, and I would say it was my friend’s car,” he added. Ilıcalı also narrated how he once helped Amokachi reach Istanbul in time for a crucial Besiktas fixture against Fenerbahce, despite supporting the latter club. According to him, Amokachi was missing in the days leading up to the derby, leaving the Besiktas coach repeatedly asking about the striker’s whereabouts. On the morning of the match, Amokachi eventually contacted Ilıcalı and disclosed that he had missed his flight and was stranded in London. The Hull City owner admitted that he initially hesitated to inform Besiktas officials because he knew the Nigerian forward could pose a serious threat to his boyhood club. “I asked Daniel where he was, and he said he had missed the flight. I switched the phone off. If I had told the Besiktas directors, they would have brought him by private jet. But Besiktas were playing Fenerbahce, and I am a Fenerbahce fan,” he recalled. However, after considering his position, Ilıcalı decided to inform a Besiktas director, who arranged a private jet to bring Amokachi to Istanbul. The striker arrived at the airport about an hour before the match and was at the stadium roughly 30 to 40 minutes before kick-off. Despite the late arrival, Amokachi made an immediate impact, scoring in the 20th minute of the game. Amokachi joined Besiktas from Everton and made a significant impression during his time in Turkey, recording 25 goals and 23 assists in 112 appearances across all competitions. item.title: US Stocks Surge After Last Week’s Losses, Nvidia +33%
item.description: Wall Street stocks bounced early Monday after last week’s bruising losses, with Nvidia rocketing about 33 percent higher as the artificial intelligence company reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Major indices had lost between seven and 10 percent last week in a rout that began with chip companies and extended more broadly. But investors engaged in bargain hunting at the start of a holiday-abbreviated week, with the Nasdaq leading major indices thanks in part to Nvidia’s jump. About 35 minutes into trading, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 2.8 percent at 49,499.93. The broad-based S&P 500 gained 4.7 percent to 7231.63, while the tech-rich Nasdaq Composite Index jumped 6.6 percent to 24,107.54. This combo photo shows the Nvidia logo and CEO Jensen Huang at a press conference with Japanese multinational information and communications technology company Fujitsu in Tokyo on July 16, 2026. Photo by PHILIP FONG / AFP Nvidia’s bombshell announcement came about 30 minutes before stock exchange opened. Futures had already been signaling a rebound session, but gains increased after Nvidia brought back Huang following input from senior US government officials that left its board confident Huang posed no national security risk. Briefing.com analyst Patrick O’Hare said the factors that have pressured stocks in recent weeks are still present, including worries about how to finance the artificial intelligence buildout, which has exacerbated inflation and boosted the odds of Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. “Those things will come back into focus, but they’re being set aside given the giddiness of the Jensen Huang news,” O’Hare said. item.title: ‘It wasn’t me’, APC chair disowns letter asking INEC to ensure Tinubu’s victory
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: National Chairman of the ruling All Progressives Congress APC, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, has denied writing the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC to ensure President Bola Tinubu is declared winner of the 2027 presidential election. He said he did not author the letter which is now circulating on social media. His spokesman said the document “did not emanate from Professor Yilwatda, was not authored by him, and has absolutely nothing to do with the National Chairman or his office.” In a statement signed by Mr Abimbola Tooki, Special Adviser to the National Chairman of APC (Media and Information Strategy), the party leader described the letter as “a fraudulent document, a malicious fabrication and a reckless attempt to impugn the integrity of the National Chairman, the APC and the democratic process.” The purported letter, addressed to the Chairman of INEC and dated November 22, 2026, is titled “Preparations for the 2027 Presidential Election and Ensuring the Victory of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.” The APC said it contains “an outrageous and entirely fabricated claim that the APC leadership expects INEC to deploy its institutional mechanisms, administrative frameworks and operational capacities to ensure the declaration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as the winner of the 2027 presidential election. “The absence of a signature is particularly telling. It is a glaring indication of the writer’s lack of credibility, accountability and seriousness, and reinforces the suspicion that the document was deliberately concocted to mislead the public, provoke needless controversy and damage the reputation of the Party’s National Chairman,” the statement said. It added that the author “has demonstrated a disturbing level of irresponsibility, dishonesty and desperation by attempting to manufacture a scandal around the APC leadership and the nation’s electoral institution.” The APC also said the letter breaks with the party’s own procedures. “It is inconceivable that a communication of such grave significance would be issued by the National Chairman outside the established channels and procedures of the Party,” the statement said. It challenged those behind the document to identify themselves. “We condemn the author of this despicable letter in the strongest possible terms and challenge those responsible to come out of hiding, take ownership of their actions and provide verifiable evidence for their claims, rather than hiding behind anonymity to spread falsehoods and create distrust in democratic institutions,” it said. item.title: Bayelsa, Rivers peace will attract investors, says AIG
item.description: …Assures residents of free, fair 2027 elections By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa YENAGOA — The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 16, Regina Udoette, has said the prevailing peace and security in Bayelsa and Rivers states will attract investors and boost economic activities. Udoette, the 13th AIG to head the zone, made the declaration during a familiarisation visit to the Bayelsa State Police Command, where she commended the leadership of the police commands in both states for their efforts in maintaining security. She said the relative stability in the two states showed that the police, other security agencies and state governments had created an enabling environment for businesses and investments to thrive. According to her, the security arrangements in the states reflected the commitment of the Commissioners of Police, state governments and other stakeholders to promoting economic growth. “Rivers and Bayelsa are safe for everyone to work and invest,” she said. On the 2027 general elections, the AIG assured residents of Bayelsa and Rivers that the Nigeria Police Force, in collaboration with other security agencies, would ensure a free and fair electoral process. She said security personnel would remain neutral and non-partisan throughout the exercise, warning that officers found violating the directive would face severe disciplinary action. “The 2027 election is not the first election to be supervised by the Nigerian Police. In 2023, the performance of the Nigerian Police and other security agencies was commended by election observers. We will also deliver on the 2027 poll,” she said. Earlier, the Bayelsa State Commissioner of Police, Ajao Saka Adewale, said the state’s geographical peculiarities posed significant policing challenges, particularly in the areas of accessibility, surveillance and rapid response. He explained that Bayelsa comprises 25 per cent landmass and 75 per cent water, with 28 police divisions and five tactical teams. Despite the challenges, Adewale said the command had sustained efforts to tackle security threats, particularly cultism and drug-related crimes, through proactive and intelligence-driven policing. He said the command had also strengthened inter-agency collaboration, increased police visibility and deepened engagement with communities. Giving an account of the command’s recent operations, Adewale disclosed that a kidnapped victim had been rescued and a suspected kidnapper arrested since he assumed office on August 12, 2026. “Between September 23, 2026 and October 8, 2026, the command arrested 24 cultists and all have been arraigned in court,” he said. He added that the command had recovered eight firearms, comprising two locally made pistols, three Beretta pistols and three locally made revolver pistols. item.title: Atiku to APC: Stop turning Zaria into hunting ground for ADC members
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has warned the All Progressives Congress (APC) against turning Tudun Wada, Zaria, into a hunting ground for opposition members following reports of the arrest of three African Democratic Congress (ADC) members and the son of another party member. Atiku said the reported arrests, particularly the alleged detention of a man’s son after police officers failed to find his father, raised serious concerns about the use of law enforcement to intimidate political opponents. In a statement by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said the three ADC members were reportedly in the custody of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), while officers searching for Isma’il Sahabi allegedly arrested his son. “If Sahabi’s son was arrested because the authorities could not find his father, he must be released immediately. A child is not a substitute for his father. No government that respects the law should tolerate the detention of one person to pressure another,” Atiku said. He demanded that the police disclose the whereabouts of the detainees, explain the allegations against them and grant them access to their families and lawyers. “Anyone against whom there is no lawful case must be released. If there is evidence of an offence, let the authorities present it before a court. An ADC membership card is not a criminal charge,” he said. Atiku also warned that the reported arrests would not stop the Affordable Life campaign, which he described as a movement driven by Nigerians struggling to afford basic necessities. “The Affordable Life campaign is a movement of Nigerians who can no longer afford fuel, food, transport or the basic necessities of daily life. Its strength comes from the hardship people experience and their determination to change it. “You cannot arrest that hardship out of existence. You cannot detain a family’s demand for relief,” he said. The former vice president urged those behind the reported arrests to end the alleged intimidation, insisting that residents of Tudun Wada had the right to support the ADC without fear. “The Affordable Life movement will continue, peacefully and resolutely, from Zaria to every part of Nigeria,” he said. item.title: Shettima tasks stakeholders on drug control master plan
item.description: …NDLEA records 77,736 arrests, 14,200 convictions under outgoing plan By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — Vice-President Kashim Shettima has charged federal and state governments, the National Assembly, private sector operators and other stakeholders to ensure the effective implementation of the National Drug Control Master Plan (NDCMP) 2026–2030. Shettima said the five-year plan required urgency, discipline and accountability from all stakeholders, warning that drug control must remain a national priority. He spoke on Monday at the official launch of the plan in Abuja, where he was represented by the Special Adviser to the President on Special Duties, Office of the Vice-President, Dr Modibbo Aliyu Umar. The Vice-President, who commended the document to relevant institutions on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, said Nigeria could not secure its future without protecting its people from the dangers of drug abuse and trafficking. He described the drug problem as a public health concern, security threat, development challenge and economic issue, stressing that enforcement alone could not address the situation without prevention, treatment and action against illicit financial flows sustaining drug markets. “Our response must therefore be comprehensive, coordinated and sustained,” he said. Shettima outlined the six pillars of the plan as supply reduction; drug demand reduction; access to controlled medicines for scientific and medical purposes; alternative development and sustainable livelihoods; disruption of the illicit drug economy; and governance, financing and coordination. He commended the leadership of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), under Brig.-Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), for introducing an Alternative Development programme, which he said was the first of its kind by a drug control agency in Africa. He noted that the programme’s pilot was already making an impact in three communities in Ondo State, urging state and local governments to support and take ownership of the initiative. On funding, the Vice-President warned that the plan could become ineffective without a credible financing framework. “A national plan without a credible financing pathway risks becoming a declaration of good intentions,” he said. He directed ministries, departments and agencies to incorporate the plan’s priorities into their institutional work plans, budget proposals and implementation schedules. Shettima also urged stakeholders to identify their respective responsibilities in ensuring the plan’s success, stressing that global complexities should not become an excuse for inaction. “Five years from now, the significance of today’s launch will not be judged by the ceremony. Let this be the moment Nigeria moves from policy to action,” he said. item.title: FCTA upgrades 20 PHCs, says pregnant women to get ambulance in 4 mins
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Capital Territory Administration FCTA has upgraded 20 primary health centres across the territory, declaring that it has cut emergency ambulance response to pregnant women to less than four minutes. Mandate Secretary, FCT Health Services and Environment Secretariat, Dr Adedolapo Fasawe, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja at the community engagement and inauguration of the renovated and upgraded Owner-Occupier Model Primary Health Centre PHC, Kubwa. She said the upgrade was carried out under the World Bank-supported Immunisation Plus and Malaria Progress by Accelerating Coverage and Transforming Services IMPACT project. To demonstrate how the emergency system works, Fasawe asked a pregnant woman to call one of the emergency lines. The ambulance reached the scene in less than four minutes. She said emergency response had been strengthened through the FCT Emergency Medical Services and Ambulance System (FEMSAS), which operates 24 hours a day, is free of charge, and brings local transport operators into the system to convey pregnant women during emergencies. According to her, the intervention goes beyond physical renovation. The administration has also built staff accommodation, provided modern medical equipment and installed solar-powered systems to guarantee 24-hour electricity and round-the-clock service. “The PHC is usually the first port of call for most residents. This is fundamental to improving health outcomes, reducing preventable deaths, and achieving universal health coverage. “This is just one of 20 primary healthcare centres across different communities in the FCT that were upgraded under the IMPACT project,” she added. On affordability, she said at least 1,000 vulnerable residents were being registered free of charge on the spot into the FCT Health Insurance Scheme under the Basic Health Care Provision Fund. The enrolment, she explained, entitles them to one year of free medical care in accredited public and private hospitals. Fasawe also commended the Minister of the FCT, Nyesom Wike, for road construction and rehabilitation projects across the satellite towns, which she said had drastically reduced travel time to health facilities. She said the administration’s healthcare intervention rests on three pillars, which are access, affordability and quality, in line with the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu. Fasawe urged traditional rulers and community leaders to take ownership of the upgraded facilities, monitor service delivery and make sure patients are not charged for free services. “Healthcare should not be a luxury reserved for a few. Quality healthcare is your fundamental human right,” she said. item.title: Democrats fire starting gun on 2028 White House race
item.description: Democrats fired the starting gun Monday on the race to win back the White House, announcing plans for 12 debates to pick their standard bearer for 2028 as the party looks to build on its sweeping midterm election victory. The first debate is scheduled for June next year, setting the stage for what could be a crowded contest to select a challenger to the Republicans, who must find a successor to term-limited President Donald Trump. The announcement comes as Democrats celebrate their biggest majority in the House of Representatives since the early 1990s, with their victories this month transforming the balance of power in Washington and raising expectations for the next two years. “Democrats are on offense after our historic victories in the midterms, and the DNC is keeping our foot on the gas as we head into the 2028 cycle,” Democratic National Committee chairman Ken Martin said. The party will hold five debates in 2027 and seven in 2028, the final one scheduled for March of that year. The debates will help voters choose the party’s presidential nominee through a series of state-by-state primary elections and caucuses, in which supporters select the candidate they want to face the Republican nominee in November 2028. Under new rules announced Monday, candidates seeking a place on the debate stage must pledge to denounce spending on their behalf by outside political groups, including those that do not disclose their donors. The requirement is intended to curb the influence of wealthy donors and so-called “dark money” in Democratic nomination contests, a longstanding demand of the party’s progressive wing. With a potentially large field, some debates could be spread across two nights, with a maximum of 20 candidates participating. No major Democrat has formally entered the race, but maneuvering is already underway among politicians seeking to become the party’s standard-bearer. Gavin Newsom, Josh Shapiro and Andy Beshear — the governors of California, Pennsylvania and Kentucky, respectively — are among those attracting attention as possible contenders. item.title: 2027 polls: Rigging could push Nigeria into civil war, says Gbenga Hashim
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Accord Party, Dr. Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has warned that any attempt to rig the 2027 general election could plunge Nigeria into a civil war. Hashim gave the warning during an interview on Symfoni Podcast, hosted by Olawale Oluwade, at the weekend, where he spoke on the state of the nation, insecurity and the credibility of the electoral process. He said Nigeria was already facing a dangerous combination of insecurity, political mistrust and weaknesses in the electoral system, which could create opportunities for armed non-state actors to exploit any post-election crisis. “The moment there’s a slight political crisis, the militia and terrorist groups, who are well organised, may take advantage of the political instability to expand and declare control in some states in the North and they will begin to press towards Abuja,” he said. The Accord Party candidate also criticised President Bola Tinubu’s handling of national crises, alleging that the President had repeatedly failed to remain in the country and confront challenges directly. “And President Tinubu will do the usual thing he does best, which is to run away. He is always away, he cannot stay to solve any problem; he will run away, he will take a flight out of the country,” Hashim said. He identified allegations that millions of fake names and artificial intelligence-generated photographs had been loaded into the Independent National Electoral Commission’s voters’ register as part of the concerns threatening the credibility of the 2027 elections. Hashim also questioned INEC’s level of preparedness less than two months before the election, while faulting the decision to postpone the clean-up of the voters’ register until after the polls. He warned that conducting the election amid rising insecurity and political violence, coupled with alleged electoral manipulation, could undermine the legitimacy of the government that would emerge from the exercise. “With the current insecurity, political violence and adding election rigging in 2027 will delegitimize the government completely and this could open space for non-state actors, insurgents, etc., already operating in 17 out of the 19 northern states to take advantage of the situation,” he warned. According to him, governors in most of the affected states have lost effective control of some rural communities, with insurgents allegedly imposing taxes on residents in areas under their influence. He said the development demonstrated the organisational capacity and financial resources available to the armed groups, warning that any political instability arising from the 2027 elections could further strengthen their operations. item.title: [UPDATED] Nvidia Board Reinstates Jensen Huang As CEO
item.description: Nvidia on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, less than two weeks after its embattled co-founder resigned over an affair with a woman US intelligence agencies suspect of spying for China. (FILES) Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang gives a thumbs up at a press conference with Japanese multinational information and communications technology company Fujitsu in Tokyo on July 16, 2026. (Photo by Philip FONG / AFP) President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.” The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, chief executive, and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead,” the company said in a statement. Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board. The decision came three days after Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Huang back, calling him “one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world” and saying he would “love to see Jensen be given a second chance.” Trump described Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions,” and said the company should rehire him “if they were smart.” Huang had offered to return, but the board initially refused. Board chair Harvey Jones had said on an earnings call last week that directors had unanimously accepted his resignation and did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family. “I can’t wait to get back to work.” Huang, 63, stepped down on November 12 following reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips. US intelligence services reportedly concluded she passed information to Beijing, which has denied the allegations. Board chair Harvey Jones said Monday that directors now believe Huang “is the right person to lead Nvidia” and that his return serves the interests of shareholders, employees, partners and customers. Jones, a former Synopsys chief executive who was named Nvidia’s first-ever board chair during the crisis, will stay in the role. Chief financial officer Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, will continue as CFO. Nvidia said a committee of independent directors set up earlier this month to investigate whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort will see its probe through to the end. Huang supports the investigation and has committed to cooperating, the company said. Shares of Nvidia rocketed about 30 percent higher in pre-market trading Monday as the tech giant announced it reinstated Huang. item.title: France Detains Three Over Mystery Train Accident
item.description: French police on Monday arrested three people at a traveller camp in connection with the September derailment of a train that injured 44 people, two sources with knowledge of the matter said. In France, the term “travellers” refers to communities who maintain an itinerant lifestyle, including some of Romani origin. The train, carrying 186 passengers, derailed on September 11 between the cities of Rouen and Caen in Normandy, northwestern France. Railway workers work on the removal of a derailed train carriage in Cleon, northwestern France, on September 16, 2026. Photo by GUILLAUME SALIGOT / AFP Prosecutors at the time said the driver had tested negative for alcohol or drugs and that a section of rail found on the track may have caused the derailment. A local official said the fragment weighed around 300 kilograms. Police on Monday detained a 45-year-old and his 22-year-old twin sons at the camp near the site of the accident, one of the sources told AFP. They were taken into police custody on suspicion of attempted theft, theft committed by a group, and involuntary bodily injury, the source said. After the derailment, President Emmanuel Macron warned of the growing threat posed by Moscow’s shadow operations across Europe, saying he had ordered measures to protect France’s critical infrastructure. item.title: War: Iran Seeks $290bn In Damages Against US
item.description: Iranian courts have demanded that the United States pay $290 billion in damages, a judiciary official said on Monday. “We have secured court rulings in domestic courts awarding $290 billion in damages against the Americans,” said Hassan Abdolianpour, head of the judiciary’s centre for lawyers, according to state television. He also said that several lawsuits have been filed against the Gulf Arab nations for “allowing their territory to be used by America to launch attacks against Iran”. According to state TV, the damages cover US actions going back decades. File photo showing US-Iran flags. The Middle East war began on February 28 when the United States and Israel launched a wave of strikes that killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iran responded by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, saying it is targeting US-Israeli bases and assets in those countries. The Islamabad memorandum of understanding signed in June between the US and Iran, which aimed to pave the way to a peace deal, included a clause that would see Washington and its regional partners drawing up a plan with at least $300 billion “for the reconstruction and economic development” of Iran. Moreover, Iran has been under crippling sanctions by the United States for decades, mainly over its nuclear program. item.title: Scramble To Save Climate Fight After COP Collapse
item.description: Officials voiced dismay on Monday at the collapse of UN climate talks, urging the world not to abandon joint efforts to curb the deadly warming of the planet. A final agreement was rejected on Sunday at the COP31 climate summit, with delegates failing to strike an agreement over fossil fuels amid resistance from oil-producing countries. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres voiced “profound frustration” while key player China expressed disappointment — but insisted the green transition was “irreversible”. COP31 President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Murat Kurum (C) attends a plenary session of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Centre, in Antalya on November 22, 2026. The EU issued a plea to salvage multilateral efforts to fight climate change, which is worsening the risk and impact of deadly storms, floods and droughts. “It is absolutely crucial that the multilateral process stays alive,” said European Commission spokeswoman Anna-Kaisa Itkonen, calling the talks’ failure a “terrible outcome”. Familiar fault lines emerged at COP31 over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas. Oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels in the final deal at the conference co-hosted by Turkey and Australia. Negotiations chair Chris Bowen who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”. Geopolitical worries Australian Minister for Climate Change and Energy and President of COP31 Negotiations Chris Bowen (C) and COP31 President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Murat Kurum (3rd R) and delegates before a session during the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Center, in Antalya, on November 22, 2026. Photo by YASIN AKGUL / AFP Bowen, Australia’s climate minister, said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory”, as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity. Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from heatwaves in Europe to floods in Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis. Faced with oil producers’ resistance, Ireland’s climate minister Darragh O’Brien vowed: “We will not endorse a cover decision … that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change.” O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, added: “We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel.” Panama, Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands also objected and as the deal imploded, COP31 became the longest climate summit on record, running two days past schedule. item.title: England Launches World’s Largest AI-Aided Breast Cancer Screening Trial
item.description: England’s state-run health service said Monday it has launched the world’s largest AI-assisted breast cancer screening trial, which is set to involve nearly 700,000 women over the next three years. The National Health Service (NHS) hailed the new trial as having the potential to transform breast cancer diagnosis, as it announced hundreds of women had been invited to take part at the outset. The £10 million ($13 million) programme will assess if tools assisted by artificial intelligence can help improve early cancer detection in screening, which health officials hope will then free up specialist clinicians’ time. The AI-assisted reading tool will assist clinicians in reviewing images collected from routine mammograms, according to the NHS. “This is the biggest AI breast cancer trial in the world,” Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said in a statement, lauding the tech’s “huge potential” while pledging “proper safeguards” to ensure safety and effectiveness. “If successful, this technology could help women get a breast cancer diagnosis and start treatment much more quickly, giving them the best possible chance of recovery.” The trial is being led by the University of Warwick, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, working closely with NHS England. (FILES) A patient is pictured before a mammography, on October 9, 2017 at the Paoli-Calmette institute in Marseille, France. A new treatment nearly halves the risk of disease progression or death from a less common form of breast cancer that hasn’t seen major drug advances in over a decade, researchers reported on June 2, 2025. (Photo by ANNE-CHRISTINE POUJOULAT / AFP) | ANNE-CHRISTINE POUJOULAT / AFP Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out. The NHS stressed screening appointments will proceed as normal, but the AI-assisted tool will be used alongside specialists checking the images to look for cancers that are too small to see or feel. The trial will test whether AI-assisted tools could allow most images to be reviewed by only one specialist, rather than the current two. Recruitment has started at Cambridge University Hospitals, in eastern England, with more of the 30 selected sites opening in the coming months. Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women, with around 55,000 diagnosed every year in the UK. Women aged 50 to 71 are invited for screening every three years, amounting to around 2.1 million screenings annually. The NHS estimates this helps prevent around 1,300 deaths. A study published in The Lancet medical journal in January said that AI can improve breast cancer detection through more effective screening while reducing radiologists’ workloads.
